title: Symphony No. 1 in D major, “Classical”
hook: Haydn as he might have written in 1917, composed in a summer of revolution.

painting.title: Lady in Blue
painting.pairingNote: A modern Petersburg painter poses his sitter in an old-fashioned gown, with strollers in period dress in the park behind her; an older elegance seen through modern eyes, as in the symphony.

facts: Prokofiev started the symphony in 1916 and finished it on 10 September 1917, the year of the two Russian revolutions. He wrote much of it in the summer of 1917 in the countryside, away from the street fighting in Petrograd.
It was an experiment: for the first time he composed without a piano, working the music out in his head. He chose a simple, classical model to make the exercise easier.

The model was Haydn, whose music he had studied in his conducting classes. In Prokofiev’s own account, he wrote as Haydn might have done had he lived in Prokofiev’s day. The nickname “Classical” is his own.
The orchestra is the size Haydn would have known: pairs of woodwind, horns and trumpets, timpani and strings. The whole symphony lasts about a quarter of an hour.
Prokofiev himself conducted the premiere in Petrograd in April 1918, shortly before he left Russia. It became one of his most popular works.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a fast, bright opening (I), a floating song (II), a stately dance with a stumble (III), a finale that never touches a minor chord (IV).

movements.heading: Allegro
movements.summary: A fast, light [[sonata-form|sonata form]] in the spirit of Haydn: two contrasting themes, a short [[development|development]] and a [[recapitulation|recapitulation]]. Prokofiev’s own fingerprints are the sudden slips into unexpected keys, which the music corrects as if nothing had happened, and the comic leaps of the second theme.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: after a quick rising flourish, a bright, bouncing tune in the violins.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a comic tune with enormous leaps in the violins, from very high to very low, over a tiptoeing bassoon.

stops.hear: A quick rising flourish from the whole orchestra, then the violins dash off with a bright, bouncing tune
The flute takes over, quick and light; then the music lurches into a new key without warning
The violins leap from very high to very low and back, delicately, while a bassoon tiptoes underneath
The opening tune again, but darker and gruffer, tossed between the instruments
The rising flourish and the bouncing tune return
The leaping violin tune once more, now in the home key

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A quick, loud close

notice: Listen for the moments when the music seems to slip on a banana skin into a strange key, then steps straight back. That is Prokofiev winking at Haydn.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Claudio Abbado recorded the symphony with the young Chamber Orchestra of Europe in Vienna in 1986; a small orchestra, close to the size Prokofiev wrote for. On the Spotify album the symphony is tracks 13–16, after *Peter and the Wolf* narrated by Sting.

movements.heading: Larghetto
movements.summary: A gentle slow movement. After a few soft chords, the first violins enter very high with a long, floating melody. The middle grows busier and louder, then the melody returns and the movement fades as it began.

mainIdeas.name: The melody
mainIdeas.description: a long, high, delicate tune in the first violins.

mainIdeas.name: The accompaniment
mainIdeas.description: soft, regular steps in the lower strings, like a slow walk.

stops.hear: A few soft chords, then the first violins enter very high and quiet with a long, floating melody
stops.happening: The main theme, in A major

stops.hear: The melody continues over light, regular steps in the lower strings
Busier: short, crisp figures pass around the orchestra and the music grows louder
The high violin melody returns

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The soft opening chords again, fading away

notice: Notice how high the violins play the melody. It gives the movement its weightless, slightly unreal sound.

movements.heading: Gavotta: Non troppo allegro
movements.summary: The shortest movement, under a minute and a half: a gavotte, an old French court dance. It begins stately and polite, then swerves into far-off keys before landing safely home. A softer middle section sits over a held bass note, like a bagpipe.

mainIdeas.name: The gavotte
mainIdeas.description: a dignified tune with big leaps and sudden swerves.

stops.hear: A stately dance with big leaps; it wanders into strange keys and lands back home with a bump
Softer: a gentle woodwind tune over a long-held low note
The gavotte returns, quieter, as if from further away

stops.label: Last 10 seconds
stops.hear: The dance tiptoes away to almost nothing

notice: Count how often the gavotte tune swerves into a key it should not be in, and how quickly it gets home.

movements.heading: Finale: Molto vivace
movements.summary: A finale at top speed, again in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]. Prokofiev threw away his first finale as too heavy and wrote this one so that, as he noted in his diary, it contains no minor chords at all. Only the second theme survives from the discarded version.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a whirling, scurrying tune in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a cheeky, skipping tune in the woodwind, with the flute racing on top.

stops.hear: A loud chord, then the strings race off with a whirling tune
The woodwind answer with a cheeky, skipping tune; the flute dashes along above
stops.happening: Theme 2, kept from the discarded first finale

stops.hear: The tunes are tossed between instruments and pushed through new keys
The whirling opening tune returns

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: A final rush and loud D major chords

notice: Listen for a minor chord. You will not find one: the whole movement stays bright.

threads.title: Old forms, new tricks
threads.body: Every movement uses a form Haydn would recognise; every movement also has Prokofiev’s sudden key-slips and wide leaps.

threads.title: Small orchestra, sharp colours
threads.body: With no trombones or tuba, the woodwind solos, especially flute and bassoon, stand out clearly.

threads.title: Neoclassical
threads.body: The symphony is often called an early example of [[neoclassicism|neoclassicism]]: modern composers returning to the clarity and forms of the eighteenth century.
